title: Git & GitHub: A Beginner’s Guide with Essential Commands
excerpt: Start version control in minutes: install Git, configure, commit, branch, and push to GitHub with the most-used commands.
html:
Version control lets you track changes, experiment safely, and collaborate. This quick guide gets you productive with Git and GitHub using the most common commands.

Install and configure Git

Download: git-scm.com/downloads

git --version

# Your identity
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

# Defaults (recommended)
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
# Windows: normalize line endings
git config --global core.autocrlf true

Initialize a new repository

mkdir my-project && cd my-project
git init

echo "# My Project" > README.md

git status
# Stage and commit your first file
git add README.md
git commit -m "Initial commit"

Clone a repository

git clone https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git
cd REPO

Everyday Git workflow

# See what changed
git status

# Stage changes
git add <file>        # stage one file
git add .               # stage everything modified/new

# Save a snapshot
git commit -m "Describe your change"

# Inspect history & changes
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all
git diff                 # unstaged changes
git diff --staged        # staged changes

# Undo (safe & common)
git restore <file>           # discard unstaged changes
git restore --staged <file>  # unstage

# Move / delete tracked files
git mv old-name new-name
git rm path/to/file

Branching and merging

# Create and switch to a new branch
git switch -c feature/idea

# List branches
git branch

# Switch back to main
git switch main

# Merge a finished feature into main
git merge feature/idea

Sync with GitHub remotes

Create a repository on GitHub, then connect and push:

# Add a remote named "origin"
git remote add origin https://github.com/USER/REPO.git
# or SSH: git remote add origin git@github.com:USER/REPO.git

# Verify remotes
git remote -v

# First push (sets upstream)
git push -u origin main

# Get latest changes
git pull                 # fetch + merge current branch
git fetch origin         # fetch without merging

# Push a feature branch
git push -u origin feature/idea

Stash work-in-progress

git stash push -m "wip: refactor"
git stash list
git stash pop

Tag releases

git tag v1.0.0
git push origin v1.0.0

Ignore files with .gitignore

echo "node_modules/" >> .gitignore
git rm -r --cached node_modules
git commit -m "Add .gitignore"

Get help

git help <command>
git <command> -h

Docs: Git • GitHub
